criteria.title: Distinguish buffering, visibility, and durable storage claims.

passages: RETURN VALUE; ERRORS EINTR/EAGAIN/EPIPE; NOTES short transfers and durability

criteria.task: Draw separate application-buffer, kernel-visible, file-synchronized and directory-synchronized states for a temporary replacement. Inject fsync EIO after a successful write and preserve the failure in the result record.
criteria.purpose: Successful write, fflush or rename is universal durable success.

knowledge: Retained T23.12 teaching passage and parent prerequisites
Active C17 semantics kept separate from POSIX/Linux, ISA, ABI and selected board contracts
artifacts: PR-T23-05 learner-owned implementation or diagnostic dossier

reasoning: Successful write, fflush or rename is universal durable success. Refute this explanation with the smallest relevant state or execution.
State valid inputs, operation pre/postconditions, object ownership/lifetime and failure/publication boundaries for the specified mechanism.
Account for resource bounds and progress/complexity under the declared participant, storage and target assumptions. Name genuinely inapplicable costs instead of inventing them.

deliverables.D1: Pre-experiment prediction and causal argument addressing: Successful write, fflush or rename is universal durable success.
deliverables.D2: Draw separate application-buffer, kernel-visible, file-synchronized and directory-synchronized states for a temporary replacement. Inject fsync EIO after a successful write and preserve the failure in the result record.
deliverables.D3: Exact commands or derivation steps, original inputs, observed outputs, a minimized disagreement and an independent control for this leaf. Retain unsupported-tool/target outcomes separately.
deliverables.D4: Replace a regular file with a pipe and show why the same synchronization API is inapplicable.
